children: Nestle India reported a 35.9 percent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 1,009.6 crore for the quarter ended September 2026, while revenue from operations rose 20.3 percent to Rs 6,788.3 crore. However, the company's shares plunged nearly 7 percent on Thursday as management flagged rising inflation, particularly food inflation, and continued commodity cost pressures.

On a standalone basis, Nestle India's net profit rose 36.2 percent year-on-year to Rs 1,026.8 crore, while revenue from operations increased 20.3 percent to Rs 6,788.3 crore. The standalone profit exceeded CNBC-TV18's poll estimate of Rs 1,018 crore, while revenue was broadly in line with the estimate of Rs 6,789 crore.
Nestle India shares fell 6.7 percent to Rs 1,291 in afternoon trade.
Nestle India Q2 results: Strong volume growth, EBITDA margin at 23.8%

Nestle India Chairman and Managing Director Manish Tiwary said the company recorded broad-based growth across product groups, supported by robust double-digit volume growth. Total sales rose 20.5 percent to Rs 6,782.2 crore, while domestic sales increased 20.4 percent.

The company's EBITDA margin stood at 23.8 percent during the quarter, even as advertising and marketing expenditure surged 46 percent as Nestle stepped up investments in its brands.
Nestle India flags food inflation, commodity cost pressures

"Rising inflation, particularly food inflation, is a reality," Tiwary said, adding that the company would focus on innovation, productivity improvements and operational efficiencies to mitigate commodity cost pressures.

In its commodity outlook, Nestle India said coffee and wheat prices were expected to remain range-bound, while sugar and edible oil prices had stabilised at elevated levels. Cocoa prices remained volatile due to weather-related concerns in major producing regions.
Milk prices have strengthened seasonally but are expected to ease with the arrival of flush supplies, the company said.
Quick commerce, organised retail support growth

Nestle India reported strong growth in its e-commerce business, led by continued momentum in quick commerce, supported by improved product availability and channel-specific product offerings. Organised retail also delivered strong growth across key categories, aided by improved in-store execution, consumer promotions and network expansion.

The company's out-of-home business benefited from innovation and premiumisation across beverages and food products, while exports maintained strong double-digit growth, supported by product launches and expansion into international markets.
